promptTemplate:
Create a NEW illustration of a small traditional Korean detached guest annex (별당, byeoldang) in exactly the same illustrated-map style as the attached reference building (a hanok estate map: LOW-POLY FACETED planes -- every surface is broken into flat angular colour facets like folded paper, NO drawn outlines, matte finish, subtle hanji paper grain, warm wood/stone colours, top-left lighting, seen straight from the front in a slightly elevated view -- same camera as the reference).

CAMERA — obey this exactly, it is the single most important constraint:
Draw the building as a perfectly FRONTAL elevation with NO rotation, exactly like the other buildings on this estate map. The roof ridge must be a HORIZONTAL line straight across the image. The left and right ends of the building are the same distance from the viewer, so the stone platform reads as a straight horizontal band -- NEVER a rhombus or a diamond. You look down on the roof a little, so the roof slope is visible, but you must NOT see the left or right side wall receding into depth, and you must NOT see a corner of the building pointing at the viewer. Symmetric and straight-on, like an architectural elevation drawing.

The building: a single small one-story hanok with its own low stone platform and steps, wooden post-and-beam frame, lattice-door front wall, and a modest hipped tile roof -- visibly smaller and simpler than the reference building (this is a guest annex, not the main house), with a small covered wooden veranda (toenmaru) along the front.

The roof is ONE single connected tiled roof resting directly on the building's columns -- there must be no second roof, no floating roof fragment, and no ghosted duplicate of the roof anywhere above or beside the building.

Do not redraw the reference building; it is for style, palette, camera and lighting only. Show ONLY the byeoldang, fully finished, centred in the frame.

Flat pure #00FF00 chroma-key green background, no gradient, no ground, no cast shadow, no text, no people.

IMPORTANT COLOR: match the reference building's palette exactly -- cool grey-beige stone platform (not pink, not cream), mid walnut wood (not bright orange), slate-grey tiles. Do not brighten or desaturate.

ABSOLUTELY AVOID: smooth painterly rendering, soft gradients, watercolour blending, photorealism, glossy 3D render, black outlines, text, labels, a second building, people.

IMPORTANT: match the geometric faceted style, palette and mood of the attached reference exactly -- this must look like part of the same illustrated set.
subjectGuards: explicitly smaller/simpler than the reference (it is an annex, not a second main house)
exactly one building in frame -- reject if the model adds a second structure or a courtyard wall
hipped tile roof, not thatched or flat -- matches every other building in the estate

EXACTLY ONE ROOF. Attempt 1 (gvi_1787125523338_pu1lcj, 4cr, rejected) drew a second detached roof floating in the air above the building with green showing through it, which also pushed neonFraction to 3.8% against the 3.0% ceiling. The roof must be one connected structure sitting directly on the building's own columns -- no floating, ghosted, mirrored or duplicated roof anywhere in the frame.

FRONTAL ELEVATION ONLY. Attempt 2 (4638a3ae3090fab969dc28af7bd15aed, 4cr, rejected) passed the F-C-estate tone gate (satMean 0.386 / valMean 0.463 / neon 0.9%) but was drawn as a 3/4 rotated view with a rhombus platform, so it did not sit with sadang/daecheongmaru/sotdaeulmun, which are all straight-on elevations. Reject any rotated or corner-on camera.

placement.note: 1536x1152 master canvas. Measured 2026-08-18: this region is 0.0% occupied. gyeRoad zone (x>=1321) must stay clear.

status: APPROVED — Phase 3 P1. Jin approved generation on 2026-08-19 ("1,2,3 해주고"). One image only, then Jin reviews before any stage authoring or placement, per the plan's 1장 생성 -> 승인 -> 배치 rule.
followUp: Once approved and generated, allowlist the finished PNG in HANOK_V1_ASSET_PROVENANCE.json's allowedModelInputs, then author byeoldang_stages.json (s1_platform/s2_frame/s3_roof/s4_final per the plan's table) and a matching estate-frame-byeoldang.json frameEdit recipe -- the same 4-step pattern already proven for sotdaeulmun/haengrangchae/anchae/sadang.
